title: The long road to Ashford
lines: The party leaves Ashford at first light and takes the north road toward Ember Gate. The air is cold and smells of wet ash and dew.
Wren checks the map and says, "The road should take two days."
Cael ties his pack to the mule and says, "I will buy more rope at the first village."
By noon the road runs beside a river. A ruined mill stands on the far bank, its wheel stuck and green with moss.
Wren shades her eyes and asks, "Is that smoke from the mill chimney?"
Yes: a thin line of grey smoke rises from the chimney.
Cael wades across the river to look inside the mill.
The water is cold and numbs him to the knees. Inside, the mill is empty except for a fresh fire and a pot of stew still warm. The air smells of onions and woodsmoke.
It is salty and hot, and nothing tastes wrong.
Cael says, "The stew is safe. Wren, come and see this."
Wren searches the mill and pries at the floorboards.
One board lifts. Under it lies a brass key, stamped with a small gate and the letters EG.
Wren pockets the key and says, "EG must mean Ember Gate."
As evening falls, hoofbeats sound from the north, three riders at least.
Cael hides the mule behind the mill and draws his hatchet.
The riders stop at the river. A voice calls out, "Whoever lit that fire, come out!"
Wren calls back, "The fire was ours. What is your business?"
The lead rider answers, "We ride for the gate, and the gate is closed to strangers."
Cael asks, "Why is the gate closed?"
"The watch has been doubled since the bells stopped ringing," the rider says.
Wren says, "Share our stew, and share your news of the road."
The riders dismount. The lead rider takes off her helmet: a woman with short iron-grey hair and a pale scar across her cheek. She smells of horse and rain.
Cael stays by the door with his hand on the hatchet through the whole meal.
In the night, the scarred rider asks to see the brass key.
Wren says, "I never mentioned a key."
Wren holds the key tightly and says, "I am going to sleep with it under my pillow."
The scarred rider smiles. "That is a fine plan," she says, and the fire burns low and red.
